decisions.title: Measure native Pi UI-prompt wait time
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 local telemetry fields. Bottom line: use Pi's native ui_prompt_start/ui_prompt_end events to measure user wait instead of relying only on ask_user tool duration. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's telemetry currently classifies user wait from ask_user calls, missing native extension prompts and dialogs. Verified upstream evidence: Pi 0.84.4 documents and exports paired UI-prompt lifecycle events with duration metadata. Benefit: complete, host-owned prompt timing and more accurate active-time metrics. Cost/risk: three small telemetry fields and two listeners; nested prompts and unfinished prompts must not double count. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now.

decisions.title: Host-owned between-tool compaction, RPC, and runtime fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit native between-tool compaction, delayed overflow recovery, RPC prompt error typing, dynamic-tool guidance, and lifecycle fixes without adding adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow keeps a domain-specific compaction threshold and durable continuation owner, uses Pi's public events and RPC client, and has no conflicting private runtime import. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.84.4 changelog, public RPC types, compaction and extension docs, examples, and captured 0.84.3-to-0.84.4 artifact document these package-owned changes. Benefit: safer long tool loops and runtime behavior with no duplicate owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no additional local code.

decisions.title: Verified private workflow generation
decisions.rationale: The official stable release is translated into the complete private nine-workflow generation with no ordinary CE runtime surface.

decisions.title: Package-owned capability discovery and timeout recovery evidence
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit prompt-free agent capability discovery, timeout recovery receipts, exact host-command cwd guidance, and lifecycle/status fixes through the existing public subagent boundary. Verified project fit: ce-workflow launches fixed project-owned roles, already recovers dirty failed turns from durable Git/work-item state, and consumes terminal status without importing pi-subagents internals. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.60.0 changelog, public tool reference, workflow docs, schema/type changes, and captured 0.59.0-to-0.60.0 artifact document these surfaces. Benefit: clearer diagnostics and safer package behavior with no duplicate recovery owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local adapter.

decisions.title: Add coded capability-list preflight before fixed-role launches
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2 launch-path change. Bottom line: do not insert a second discovery RPC before every fixed-role action. Verified project fit: ce-workflow ships and selects exact project agents, while failed or disabled launches already return bounded terminal evidence and preserve the action lease. Verified upstream evidence: capabilities:true is declared/default routing discovery rather than exact task-specific preflight. Benefit: avoids an extra round trip and another launch dependency. Cost/risk: a missing agent still fails at the existing launch boundary. Confidence: high. Recommendation: use discovery only for interactive agent selection, not ce-workflow's coded fixed roles.

decisions.title: Responsive decision UI and Herdr attention signaling
decisions.rationale: Responsive list layouts and blocked/waiting attention signals are implemented inside pi-ask-user and inherited by ce-workflow's existing ask_user calls. Local dialog policy remains separate and no compatibility shim is required.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-ask-user behavior is inherited through ce-workflow's existing ask_user calls.

decisions.title: ask_user telemetry integration
decisions.rationale: The release exposes no stable per-call telemetry API, while ce-workflow already records tool timing and dialog decisions. Local wrapping would duplicate package behavior without measurable savings; revisit if a public metrics hook appears.

decisions.title: Package-owned reply routing guard and stable tool visibility
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit the active-ask reply-target guard and removal of lazy intercom tool visibility without a ce-workflow adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow already requires exact-session trust checks, pending-message inspection, and explicit reply threading; it has no toolVisibility configuration or intercom transport implementation. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.12.1 README, public tool/config behavior, and captured 0.12.0-to-0.12.1 artifact document the guard and stable active-tool policy. Benefit: safer replies and prompt-cache-stable tool schemas from the package owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code or config.

decisions.title: Independent goal safety and coexistence release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 baseline-only record and package rollback. Bottom line: record installed 0.54.3 as an independently owned goal extension; do not replace or integrate ce-workflow's domain-specific autonomous engine. Verified project fit: this repository has no pi-goal dependency or command/event callsite, while ce-workflow's goal loop owns work-item, verifier, catch-up, compaction, and completion gates. Verified upstream evidence: the captured 0.52.1-to-0.54.3 artifact and installed README document stable goal tools, safety limits, a built runtime, and cooperative workflow mutex behavior. Benefit: acknowledge the installed package's stable tools, safety limits, mutex behavior, and built runtime. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now as no-local-action.
decisions.verification: Installed @narumitw/pi-goal package manifest is 0.54.3; captured 0.52.1-to-0.54.3 README and public runtime artifact reviewed; repository search found no integration callsite

decisions.title: Replace ce-workflow autonomous goals with pi-goal
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 3 after state and command migration. Bottom line: pi-goal remains a generic single-objective loop, not a substitute for ce-workflow's work-item, verifier, catch-up, lease, and completion gates. Verified project fit: ce-workflow enforces domain state before completion and has distinct human-decision and safety paths. Verified upstream evidence: 0.54.3 exposes generic goal_complete, goal_blocked, goal_wait, and optional managed-run behavior. Benefit: avoids deleting required domain guarantees for superficial code reduction. Cost/risk: the purpose-built engine remains. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no replacement.

decisions.title: Add workflow mutex integration without a reproduced collision
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not add an optional coordination protocol without evidence that ce-workflow and pi-goal contend in supported use. Verified project fit: ce-workflow does not invoke pi-goal and the package is not a dependency. Verified upstream evidence: the mutex is cooperative and its documented coexistence guarantee is characterized for pi-goal with plan mode, not ce-workflow. Benefit: avoids speculative lifecycle state. Cost/risk: independently activated workflow extensions can still conflict if a user deliberately runs both. Confidence: high. Recommendation: revisit only with a concrete collision reproduction.

decisions.title: Goal package UI, persistence, safety, and build internals
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit package-owned tool visibility, state restoration, limits, mutex participation, and bundled runtime behavior without adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow has no pi-goal API consumer. Benefit: keeps ownership clear. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code.

decisions.title: Memory-bounded graph, diagnostics, and lifecycle reliability release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback and baseline-only edit. Bottom line: adopt installed 4.1.3 without ce-workflow source changes. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's only dedicated integration is the isolated verifier's optional read-only project_report call with compact view; immutable evidence still comes from checkpoint-scoped tools, and other durable role allowlists remain independent of this ambient extension. Verified upstream evidence: installed package metadata reports 4.1.3, and the changelog plus captured 4.1.2-to-4.1.3 artifact document the release. Benefit: inherit memory-bounded graph architecture, compact report plumbing, exact work counters, read-guard and opaque-write hardening, diagnostics bus pinning, LSP and server lifecycle fixes, and cache isolation. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure; no migration cost. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now and advance only this package's reviewed baseline.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-lens package metadata and changelog report 4.1.3; captured 4.1.2-to-4.1.3 artifact reviewed; repository search confirms the optional project_report boundary and checkpoint-scoped evidence tools

decisions.title: Add optional pi-lens tools to every durable role allowlist
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not make durable roles depend on an optional ambient extension. Verified project fit: explicit role allowlists must remain launchable without pi-lens, while the lens verifier is selected only after a coded availability check. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.3 improves package tool internals and report plumbing but does not change ce-workflow's optional dependency boundary. Benefit: preserves role availability. Cost/risk: roles continue using native targeted reads unless pi-lens is present. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the current boundary.

decisions.title: Use live graph and symbol tools as immutable checkpoint evidence
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: keep immutable findings on checkpoint-scoped verifier tools. Verified project fit: project_report supplies optional orientation, while module_report and read_symbol inspect the live workspace and cannot bind findings to a recorded checkpoint. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.3 bounds graph memory and strengthens read guards but does not make live tools checkpoint readers. Benefit: avoids time-of-check/time-of-use drift. Cost/risk: checkpoint reads remain deliberately bounded. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no verifier expansion.

decisions.title: Add a ce-workflow diagnostics-bus adapter
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not duplicate pi-lens diagnostics lifecycle ownership. Verified project fit: ce-workflow has no diagnostics event consumer and receives bounded findings through public tool results; adding an adapter would create a second warning and persistence path. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.3 pins the package's pilens:diagnostics publisher and subscriber surface but does not require downstream mediation. Benefit: retaining the package boundary avoids duplicate notifications and state. Cost/risk: an adapter would add event lifecycle and deduplication code without a current gap. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local change.

decisions.title: Package-owned scanners, parsers, LSP, graph, cache, telemetry, and runtime fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit opaque-write recovery, read-guard hardening, parser and LSP lifecycle fixes, graph compaction and eviction, cache work counters, telemetry, test isolation, and diagnostics bus governance without adapters. Verified project fit: these are implemented behind pi-lens's public tool results and diagnostics pipeline. Benefit: avoids duplicating package internals. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code.
